title: The Practical Approach To Seeking The Kingdom
paragraphs: But today we will focus on the topic of how to seek the Kingdom. The theme of this series is rediscovering the primacy of God. God's priority is very simple. It is the kingdom of God. We will discuss the practical approach to seeking or pursuing the Kingdom. If I ask you to do something without telling you how to do it, my instructions will most likely be incomplete. So when Jesus declared God's priority, it was "Seek first the kingdom." I'm sure he wanted us to know how to do that.

And I want to start by reminding us of the priority of priorities. Why are we discussing the topic of priority? The greatest challenge in life on Earth is the complex daily demands of choosing between competing alternatives within our limited time. I want you to read this sentence while you are writing it down. This, for me, is the greatest challenge on earth. It is dealing with the competing demands of alternative options that vie for our time every day.

Every morning you wake up, you have to decide which clothes to wear from that closet. Sometimes some of you spend all night doing that. Because you have a dress or suit that competes with the others. Then you move on to the shoe, and this takes another 25 to 30 minutes. Which one should I wear? Because you have a lot of them. I once asked my friend Mike Murdock, we were organizing a conference together. I said to him, "Man, you wear black all the time. Why do you always wear black?" He replied: "I get ready faster.

All my suits are black. All my shoes are black. So, when I go to the closet, I don't waste time trying to decide what to wear. I just grab a suit. It's black." However, there are many other, more important issues competing for our time. Which route will we take to work this morning? Some of you have no other way but the one you use. Which meeting should I attend? Which invitation should I accept? What will I do on my vacation? Where should I go on vacation? There is a constant demand that competes for our time.

I want you to write the following phrase, and I believe it will help you, because this is the secret of my life: life is designed to be simple, not complicated. God wanted life to be very simple. But for most people, simply deciding what to do in a single day is complicated. The third point I want to make is my solution to the problem, which is that the key to simplifying your life is setting priorities. The key to simplifying your life is setting priorities.

Usually, when I am asked by the media, wherever I am in the world, one of the common questions that is asked in their interviews with me, because I think some of them see my life and see me involved in a lot of things, they try to find out: How do you achieve balance in your life? You are a father, a husband, a shepherd, a brother to sisters, a son to a father, a civil leader, you work in the media, you write books, you travel, and you speak at conferences; You do all these things. How do you maintain balance?

What is the secret to doing all these things successfully? I gave them three answers that took me some time to come up with. I will present it to you, my secret to achieving balance. Number one, setting priorities. Number two, organization. And number three, discipline. This is how I successfully deal with the pressures of competing alternatives. I will repeat it. If you want to be successful, you have to do it. Number one is setting priorities, and that is number one in my life.

Prioritizing protects you from trying to do everything. The second is organization. Once you have identified your priorities, i. e. , the list of things that are important and valuable to you, you must organize them properly and in the appropriate order so that the most important comes first. Most important, then next most important. Prioritizing your tasks is important. For example, your priorities might be God, family, worship, work, business. You have this list, but you might be putting trade before God.

You spend more time at your work than you spend with God. So, even if you have your priorities, their order may be incorrect. Therefore, the second point is important. You need to organize your priorities. Then the third one is the most difficult. Discipline. Discipline means that once you have set your priorities, you have to discipline yourself to keep each one in its proper order. Incidentally, the word discipline, you may wish to write it, means the restrictions that one imposes on oneself.

This means imposing certain restrictions on yourself in order to achieve a desired goal. This is discipline. Self-discipline, therefore, is the highest form of governance. It is called self-governance. It means governing yourself according to your own priorities. So, the key to living life, and I want you to hear this please, as millions of people around the world listen to this program today, is that life is too complicated to have no priorities. The way to simplify life is to prioritize. What do I mean by that?

Point number four. Setting the right and appropriate priorities in life is the key to a successful and fulfilling life. Now, I wanted to underline two words here. Setting the correct and appropriate priority. My friend, listen to me. You may be choosing incorrect priorities. For example, the drug dealer's priority today, first thing, is distributing drugs, and killing some children. That is his priority. Is this the right priority for our nation?

The thief's priority is to get into your house by any means necessary. That's a priority for the thief. Is this the right priority for building our social structure as a nation? In other words, your priorities are not important just because they are priorities. You have to ask yourself, are these the right priorities? Have you chosen the right priorities? For some people, food is their priority. First thing, they want to eat. They don't want to pray first thing in the morning. They want food first.

Is this the right priority? The Bible says: “ Seek my face every day.” I will wake up early in the morning and ask for your face. Some people wake up early in the morning and look for conflicts. Therefore, the priority may be incorrect. The way to succeed in life, then, is not just about having priorities, and not just about organizing them, but you must also make sure they are the right priorities. Here is the final introductory point. Jesus set the right priority for all human beings.

And for this reason, everyone, every race, every color, every creed, every religious person watching this program and listening to this disc today or watching this digital disc, wherever you are or in this holy place, I want you to listen carefully to Jesus setting the first priority for all human beings, without exception. So, whether you are a Christian, a Buddhist, a Hindu, a Confucian, a Scientologist, or an atheist, it doesn't matter to me.

According to Christ, every human being should place this as their most important and first priority. What is that priority? He gave us only one priority worth pursuing. These two priorities were established by God. When I saw them in my life years ago, they made my life very simple. The first priority is the Kingdom of God. Order first. First means priority. Everything else comes second. The second priority he set for all human beings is the righteousness of God. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.

After that, Jesus added all the other things. Isn't this wonderful? He said, "Look, all you have to do in your life is put two things at the top, and everything else is not worth pursuing." How wonderful. He said, "Look, I want you to devote your energy, time, and attention to two things." First, the Kingdom of God, and second, the righteousness of God. In our last session, we discussed the topic of righteousness. It is very important, and so is the Kingdom. First and foremost, what is the Kingdom?

What does it mean to seek the Kingdom? Seek the kingdom. Firstly, the kingdom is the ruling influence of heaven on earth. The kingdom is a government with sovereign scope. So, when he said the kingdom of heaven, he meant the government of a place called heaven. He says: " First seek the governing influence of Heaven on Earth." Ask for it first. In your work, in your home, in your business, in your body, in your investments, in your children, in your profession, in your hobbies, in your vacation.

He said, "Whatever you do, seek the influence of heaven on earth in that domain first." Then he says: "Righteousness". "Righteousness means uprightness or proper alignment with the authority of the government." This is the meaning of the word. It doesn't mean wearing a long robe and a turban with a turned-down collar and a cross in your pocket. The word bar simply means the correct position with power or proper positioning with power. He said: "Two things are important in life, and that's all that matters in life."

He says: "Only two things." First, it seeks God's influence on Earth, and second, it seeks to remain on good terms with that government. Everything else, he says, will be added to you. Everything else will be added to you. Everything else will be added to you. What are the two things we should strive for? the first? Say it out loud. The Kingdom of God. What is the second thing we should pursue? So, what are God's priorities? The Kingdom and righteousness. What is God's priority? The Kingdom and righteousness.

What is God's priority? Say it out loud, everyone. What are God's priorities? The Kingdom and righteousness. That's all. He never said to pursue anything else. He said, “And everything after that will seek you out.” I don’t think we’ve grasped it yet. I tell you, I don’t think we’ve grasped it yet. Please listen to this simple message. In the past few months, I’ve been overwhelmed by things that were seeking me out.

This week alone—remember what I told you last Sunday—I said, “This week you will be overwhelmed if you understand the message and seek it out.” I tell you, my friends, it happened to me the very next day, Monday. Monday of this week— you’ll know about it later, God willing. But some things happened to me on Monday. I had just preached on Sunday. And the things I’ve been trying to pursue for ministry found me. I said, “God, I want you to show your power.” He said, “Only seek my kingdom.” What are God’s two priorities? What is God’s priority? Isn’t that simple? It’s amazing. God’s priority—let’s read Matthew chapter 6.

He sets your priority, and then He sets His own. Let’s set your priority first. Matthew chapter 6 begins like this in this discourse, verse 25. Read it aloud. So, come on, all of you, out loud. Therefore I say to you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food? Are you kidding God? We’re Bahamians, man. We take a second job and can’t come to prayer meetings because of food. Forgive me. But I’m just a teacher. I’m not picking anyone. You’re too young to be tired. Are you tired? " For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. Seek first. Is that more important? Here's the answer.

Rather, seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness. And what happens? All these things will be added to you. He didn't even say you have to go and search for them.
